headline: Proposed Homestead property tax exemption sent to City Council for a public hearing next month.
summary: The tax break would be a percentage of assessed value, so higher-valued homes would get a larger break. Some questions focused on whether the break should cover only the dwelling or the land too. A resident asked for a no-solicitor opt-out list, modeled on one in the town of orange.
decisions: Referred the Homestead property tax exemption ordinance to City Council, with a public hearing set for next month.
discussion: Homestead exemption scope: Members questioned whether the break should cover only the dwelling or also the land, and how the state statute applies.

Tax shift to businesses: Members raised concern that the break would move the tax burden to commercial property owners and businesses, and public speakers opposed shifting taxes to businesses and apartment buildings.
Eligibility checks and records: The approach modeled on New Milford uses driver's licenses, insurance records, and voter registration, and Stratford requires social security numbers on paper.
Solicitor opt-out list: A resident asked for an opt-out list for door-to-door solicitors, like one in the town of orange, and the group agreed to continue the conversation.
Implementation timeline: The program would need to serve about 18,000 people by December 31st of next year, which members said needs planning and resources.

decision_evidence.quote: We'll make a motion to send it to City Council to set a public hearing. ... All in favor? Aye. Aye. Motion passes.
